(1) if bgp_large_community ~ [(64512, 1, *)] then { c = filter(...).min; bgp_med = c.data2; } Action community "set MED": if the route has a community 64512:1:X, set MED = X. filter(...) keeps only the matching communities, and .min picks the lowest if there are several. data2 is the third field (X).
(2) if bgp_large_community ~ [(64512, 2, *)] then { ...; prepend_times(c.data2); } Action community "prepend N times": the originator chooses how much to make its route less preferred.
(3) bgp_local_pref = 200 - bgp_path.len * 10; Local-pref from AS path length: a shorter path gives a higher local-pref. The length is measured after the prepend in step (2), so prepending lowers local-pref.
(4) bgp_path.delete([65000..65100]); Strip an ASN range: removes all ASNs from 65000 to 65100 from the path. This removes the servers' private ASNs (65001, 65002).
(5) bgp_large_community.add((64512, 9, net.len)); Metadata community: adds 64512:9:<prefix length>, for example 64512:9:32 for a /32.
– bgp_large_community.delete([(64512, 1, *), (64512, 2, *)]); Cleanup: removes the action communities, so they are not sent further.
– accept; Send the changed route.

At the end, include "/etc/bird.d/*.conf"; loads the extra config files. You add the BGP part in that directory.

3.2 Add the BGP configuration

Open a shell on bgp-rr:

docker exec -it bgp-rr bash

The config uses a template. All settings shared by the RR clients are defined once, and each protocol bgp inherits them with from:

  • local 100.65.0.3 as 64512: source address (loopback) and local AS.
  • rr client: this neighbor is a route-reflector client.
  • rr cluster id 100.65.0.3: the cluster ID added to CLUSTER_LIST on reflected routes.
  • add paths rx: accept multiple paths per prefix from the client (R1 sends them with addpath-tx-all-paths).
  • import all: accept every route from the clients.
  • export filter export_to_clients: apply the filter from Task 3.1 to every route sent to the clients.

Add configuration:

cat  > /etc/bird.d/bgp.conf <<EOF

template bgp ibgp_rr_client {
    local 100.65.0.3 as 64512;
    rr client;
    rr cluster id 100.65.0.3;

    ipv4 {
        add paths rx;
        import all;
        export filter export_to_clients;
    };
}

protocol bgp ibgp_r1 from ibgp_rr_client {
    description "RR client R1";
    neighbor 100.65.0.1 as 64512;
}

protocol bgp ibgp_r2 from ibgp_rr_client {
    description "RR client R2";
    neighbor 100.65.0.2 as 64512;
}

EOF

3.3 Check the config and apply it

First check the syntax only (-p = parse and exit). Nothing is changed:

bird -p -c /etc/bird/bird.conf
echo $?                          # 0 = config OK

Then tell the running BIRD to load the new config. This does not restart it:

birdc configure

Expected result:

Reading configuration from /etc/bird/bird.conf
Reconfigured

3.4 Verify the BGP sessions

Wait 10 seconds for BGP to establish:

birdc show protocols
birdc show protocols all ibgp_r1

Expected result:

Name       Proto      Table      State  Since         Info
ibgp_r1    BGP        ---        up     14:24:44.172  Established
ibgp_r2    BGP        ---        up     14:24:44.447  Established
ospf_main  OSPF       master4    up     14:18:03.086  Running

3.5 What the RR received (before the filter)

Show the routes that BIRD received from R1, with all attributes:

birdc show route protocol ibgp_r1 all

Expected result: the route is exactly as www-1 sent it. BIRD resolves the next hop 10.1.0.2 recursively through OSPF (hostentry, igp_metric).

100.64.1.100/32      unicast [ibgp_r1 ... from 100.65.0.1] * (100/20) [AS65001?]
	via 10.10.0.1 on eth1
	hostentry: via 10.1.0.2 table master4
	bgp_path: 65001
	bgp_next_hop: 10.1.0.2
	bgp_local_pref: 100
	bgp_large_community: (64512, 1, 777) (64512, 2, 3)

3.6 What the RR sends to R2 (after the filter)

Show the routes that BIRD sends to R2, after the export filter:

birdc show route export ibgp_r2 all

Expected result:

100.64.1.100/32      unicast [ibgp_r1 ... from 100.65.0.1] * (100/20) [AS64521?]
	bgp_path: 64523 64522 64521
	bgp_next_hop: 10.1.0.2
	bgp_med: 777
	bgp_local_pref: 160
	bgp_large_community: (64512, 9, 32)

Step by step for www-1's route:

Step Result
in path 65001, LC (64512,1,777) (64512,2,3)
(1) MED = 777
(2) prepend 3× → path 64523 64522 64521 65001
(3) path length 4 → local-pref 200 - 40 = 160
(4) 65001 deleted → path 64523 64522 64521
(5) LC (64512,9,32) added
out the action communities are removed, only (64512,9,32) is left 
birdc show route export ibgp_r1 all

This is empty. BIRD does not send a route back to the client it came from.

Exit the remote shell using:

exit

Task 4 – Verify on R2 and test the service

Check the iBGP session to the RR and the VIP route on R2:

docker exec -it r2 vtysh -c "show bgp summary"
docker exec -it r2 vtysh -c "show bgp ipv4 unicast 100.64.1.100/32"

Expected result:

  64523 64522 64521
    10.1.0.2 (metric 20) from 100.65.0.3 (100.65.0.1)
      Origin incomplete, metric 777, localpref 160, valid, internal, best (First path received)
      Large Community: 64512:9:32
      Originator: 100.65.0.1, Cluster list: 100.65.0.3
  • The route was reflected: Originator 100.65.0.1 (R1) and Cluster list 100.65.0.3.
  • MED, local-pref, AS path and communities are the values set by the BIRD filter.
  • The next hop 10.1.0.2 (www-1) is reachable through OSPF via R1.

Test the service from R2:

docker exec -it r2 ip route get 100.64.1.100     # via 10.10.0.1 (R1)
docker exec -it r2 curl -s http://100.64.1.100/

The page must contain www-1.

Task 5 – Failover: www-1 → www-2 and back

Keep one terminal open to watch R2:

docker exec -it r2 sh -c 'while true; do curl -s --max-time 1 http://100.64.1.100/ | grep "<p>"; sleep 1; done'

5.1 Stop nginx on www-1

Stop the web server on www-1, so that its health check fails:

docker exec -it www-1 sv stop /services/nginx

Within a few seconds, the following happens:

  1. check_http on www-1 fails twice (fall 2). The priority drops from 130 to 110.
  2. www-2 (120) becomes MASTER. It takes the VIP and runs its notify_master, so GoBGP advertises the VIP with 64512:1:888,64512:2:1.
  3. www-1 becomes BACKUP. It removes the VIP and runs its notify_backup, so GoBGP withdraws the VIP.
  4. R1 → BIRD → R2: R2 now gets the route from www-2.

Verify:

docker exec -it www-1 ip -br addr show eth1      # no VIP
docker exec -it www-2 ip -br addr show eth1      # 100.64.1.100/32
docker exec -it bgp-rr birdc show route export ibgp_r2 all
docker exec -it r2 vtysh -c "show bgp ipv4 unicast 100.64.1.100/32"

Expected result on R2:

  64521
    10.2.0.2 (metric 20) from 100.65.0.3 (100.65.0.1)
      Origin incomplete, metric 888, localpref 180, valid, internal, best
      Large Community: 64512:9:32

Step by step for www-2's route: MED 888, 1 prepend → path 64521 65002 (length 2) → local-pref 200 - 20 = 180, 65002 deleted → path 64521.

The loop on R2 now prints www-2.

5.2 Start nginx on www-1 again [ optional ]

Start the web server on www-1 again:

docker exec -it www-1 sv start /services/nginx

After rise 2, www-1 is back at priority 130 and takes over again (preemption). It advertises the VIP with its own communities, and www-2 withdraws.

Verify:

docker exec -it www-1 ip -br addr show eth1      # 100.64.1.100/32
docker exec -it www-2 ip -br addr show eth1      # no VIP
docker exec -it r2 vtysh -c "show bgp ipv4 unicast 100.64.1.100/32"   # 64523 64522 64521, metric 777, localpref 160

The loop on R2 prints www-1 again. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

Troubleshooting checklist

Symptom Check
GoBGP neighbor not Establ gobgp neighbor 10.1.0.1, R1: vtysh -c "show bgp neighbors 10.1.0.2", ping 10.1.0.1
VIP on the server, but not in gobgp global rib cat /etc/keepalived.d/notify.conf, then sv restart /services/keepalived (notify runs only on a state change)
Both servers are MASTER VRRP unicast between 10.1.0.2 ↔ 10.2.0.2: ping between the servers, auth_pass and virtual_router_id must match
bird -p reports an error The error shows the file and line, usually in /etc/bird.d/bgp.conf
BIRD sessions not Established birdc show protocols all ibgp_r1, OSPF route to 100.65.0.1 (birdc show route 100.65.0.1/32)
R2 does not have the route birdc show route protocol ibgp_r1 all, birdc show route export ibgp_r2 all
Route attributes on R2 are not as expected birdc show route export ibgp_r2 all, then go through the filter steps in Task 3.1

keepalived log: docker logs www-1 2>&1 | grep Keepalived_vrrp. Use docker logs -f www-1 to follow it live.

Cleanup

Destroy the lab:

containerlab destroy -t lab5.clab.yml
